offence_severity: rigorous imprisonment for 3 years to life imprisonment
physical_harm: Deceased 'C' sustained multiple injuries upon vital parts of the body as a result of bombs being thrown at him, and his son 'K' also died after sustaining injuries
number_of_offences: Charges levied against the accused and the sentence as awarded by the Courts below not interfered with
premeditation_planning: The court found that the accused had formed an unlawful assembly and had made preparation for the murder
key_evidence_accepted: Death of the deceased 'C' and his son 'K' is undisputed – Deceased 'C' having sustained multiple injuries upon vital parts of the body as a result of the bombs being thrown at him also stands proved – Testimonies of three witnesses is coherent on material facts such as the presence of the accused on the spot of the crime; the death of the deceased; a blast having taken place; and the accused being the assailants.
witness_credibility: All 3 primary witnesses of the prosecution i.e., PW-3, PW-16, and PW-17 have categorically deposed the presence of the appellants at the spot of the crime and such a statement could not be shaken in cross-examination – The creditworthiness of the witnesses is unimpeachable.
bail_history: Bail granted to the appellants stands cancelled, to surrender
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 17.04.1988; Trial judgment: 11.05.1992; High Court decision: 19.10.2010; Supreme Court decision: 10.10.2023
legal_representation: Abhishek Vikas, Anshuman Shrivastava, Abhijeet Shrivastava, Abhishek Sharma, S. K. Verma, Advs. for the Appellants; Sumeer Sodhi, Yash Gupta, Advs. for the Respondent
investigation_status: FIR registered; charge sheet filed; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction affirmed; High Court: Conviction affirmed; Supreme Court: Appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution's case rested primarily on the testimonies of three witnesses, PW-3, PW-16, and PW-17, who categorically deposed the presence of the appellants at the crime scene, the death of the deceased, and the occurrence of a blast. The Court found these testimonies to be coherent, reliable, and unimpeachable, with no force in the contention that they were contradictory.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the prosecution's case was undermined by the delay in filing the FIR, the alleged contradictions in the testimonies of the prosecution witnesses, the deceased's history of criminal cases, and the appellants' plea of alibi. However, the Court rejected these arguments, finding the delay not fatal, the testimonies not contradictory, and the alibi not conclusively established.
legal_principle_applied: The Court applied the principle of preponderance of probability and the standard of 'strict scrutiny' for the plea of alibi. It also emphasized that the burden of proof lies with the prosecution to establish the presence of the accused at the crime scene.
precedent_relied_upon: Apren Joseph v. State of Kerala (1973) 3 SCC 114; State of M.P. v. Ratan Singh (2020) 12 SCC 630; Bhagwan Singh v. Dilip Singh alias Depak & Anr. 2023 SCC OnLine 1059; Binay Kumar Singh v. State of Bihar (1997) 1 SCC 283; Ram Jag v. State of U.P (1974) 4 SCC 201
sentencing_rationale: The sentence imposed was found to be justified as it was proportionate to the crimes committed, and the Court did not find any reason to interfere with the sentences awarded by the Trial Court and confirmed by the High Court.
other_sentence_order: Bail granted to the appellants stands cancelled, and they are directed to surrender forthwith. The concerned trial court is to take consequential steps.
